precepts.text: David's repentance after Nathan came to him: he pleads for mercy and acknowledges his transgression.
precepts.point: Yet for David's sake the Most High gives him a lamp in Jerusalem, because David did right all his days save only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite, a wrong from which David repented.

note.label: 1 Kings 15: Abijam, Asa, Nadab, and Baasha

precepts.why:
This is David’s repentance after Nathan came to him: “Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness: according unto the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions. Wash me throughly from mine iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin. For I acknowledge my transgressions: and my sin is ever before me.”

The matter of Uriah the Hittite was a real wrong, and it is the one exception the scripture names: David did right all the days of his life, “save only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.” But David pleaded for mercy and acknowledged his transgression. He repented.

That is why, for David’s sake, the Most High gave Abijam a lamp in Jerusalem, even though Abijam walked in all the sins of his father and his heart was not perfect as David’s was. The children did what they saw their fathers do; David’s heart was the standard, and his repentance is part of why.

precepts.text: Asa slept with his fathers and Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his stead.
precepts.point: He strengthened himself against Israel, setting himself apart from the northern kingdom's ways.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 17: Jehoshaphat Sends Teachers Through the Cities

precepts.why:
“And Asa slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father: and Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his stead.”

Kings tells the same succession: Jehoshaphat reigned in the place of his father Asa, taking the throne after him. And Chronicles adds what he did first: he “strengthened himself against Israel”, setting himself apart from the northern kingdom's ways.

precepts.text: Asa fortified Mizpah in his war with Baasha king of Israel, and that pit became the grave Ishmael used.
precepts.point: The pit Ishmael filled with the slain was the one Asa the king had made for fear of Baasha king of Israel during the war between them.

note.label: Jeremiah 41: Ishmael Murders Gedaliah and Johanan Recovers the Remnant

precepts.why:
The pit Ishmael filled with the eighty men he slew “was it which Asa the king had made for fear of Baasha king of Israel”. Kings shows when: “Then king Asa made a proclamation throughout all Judah; none was exempted: and they took away the stones of Ramah, and the timber thereof, wherewith Baasha had builded; and king Asa built with them Geba of Benjamin, and Mizpah.”

Asa fortified Mizpah in his war with Baasha king of Israel, with the stones and timber of Ramah. The pit dug for fear of Baasha during that war became the grave Ishmael used, when he went out from Mizpah weeping, playing a part, invited the men in to Gedaliah, and slew them in the midst of the city, sparing only the ten that had treasures of wheat, barley, oil and honey hidden in the field.

points: After Abijam dies, Asa his son reigns forty-one years and does right in the eyes of the Most High as David his father did.

note.label: 1 Kings 15: Abijam, Asa, Nadab, and Baasha

points: Asa takes the sodomites out of the land, removes the idols his fathers made, and even removes his own mother Maachah from being queen because she made an idol in a grove, which he destroys and burns at the brook Kidron.

note.label: 1 Kings 15: Abijam, Asa, Nadab, and Baasha

points: Though the high places are not removed, Asa's heart is perfect with the Most High all his days, and he brings dedicated silver, gold, and vessels into the house of the Most High.

note.label: 1 Kings 15: Abijam, Asa, Nadab, and Baasha

points: There is war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel, who builds Ramah to cut off passage to and from Asa.

note.label: 1 Kings 15: Abijam, Asa, Nadab, and Baasha

points: Asa takes silver and gold from the house of the Most High and the king's house and sends it to Benhadad of Syria to break his league with Baasha, and Benhadad smites cities of Israel so Baasha stops building Ramah.

note.label: 1 Kings 15: Abijam, Asa, Nadab, and Baasha

points: Asa uses the stones and timber of Ramah to build Geba and Mizpah. In his old age he is diseased in his feet, then sleeps with his fathers, and Jehoshaphat his son reigns in his place.

note.label: 1 Kings 15: Abijam, Asa, Nadab, and Baasha

points: Nadab son of Jeroboam reigns over Israel two years and does evil, walking in the way and sin of his father.

note.label: 1 Kings 15: Abijam, Asa, Nadab, and Baasha

points: Baasha conspires against him, kills him, and reigns in his place, then smites all the house of Jeroboam, leaving none that breathed, according to the word spoken by Ahijah the Shilonite.

note.label: 1 Kings 15: Abijam, Asa, Nadab, and Baasha

points: This fulfills, years later, the judgment that Jeroboam's descendants would be destroyed for the sins by which he made Israel to sin.
